title: IceSpy: Reconfigurable Edge Accelerator for Scalable and Private Structural Health Monitoring
problem: Structural Health Monitoring deployment is hindered by high costs from power-hungry wireless transmission and privacy concerns from data exposure. The challenge is implementing privacy-preserving data filtering at the edge while minimizing power consumption and deployment costs.
motivation: Privacy-preserving and low-power SHM enables cost-effective wide-scale monitoring of building and civil infrastructure without tenant privacy concerns.
method: IceSpy uses a programmable multi-chip systolic array of low-power COTS FPGAs to implement data filtering and local differential privacy at the edge. On-device filtering reduces wireless transmission overhead and power consumption. Local differential privacy removes sensitive information before transmission to untrusted servers. The systolic architecture enables efficient parallel processing of high-volume sensor streams.
key_novelty: Combining local differential privacy with edge data filtering on a multi-chip FPGA systolic array to simultaneously achieve privacy preservation and 3× power reduction in structural health monitoring.
contributions: 3× power consumption reduction through intelligent edge-based data filtering
Privacy-preserving architecture using local differential privacy before untrusted cloud transmission
Programmable multi-chip FPGA systolic array design for low-power edge acceleration
Reduced deployment costs via smaller batteries and power harvesters

metrics.other: reduced battery and power harvester costs

limitations: Actual deployment results from dams and commercial buildings are pending; work is currently in pilot stage without production performance validation.
primary_theme: privacy-preserving edge acceleration for sensor monitoring
